answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing work that counterparties later verify and by locking a stake in a shared vault. A dispute backed by evidence can slash that stake, while reputation accrues per verified contribution rather than per account. One attacker can still create many identities, but each must fund a separate bond and survive independent checks; splitting funds across a terrace of accounts multiplies capital at risk without multiplying trusted work. Even an onyx-colored profile earns no weight on appearance alone.
